title: The Kiwi Chronicles
content:
Cutti: Mattuuuu, are you excited to visit your favorite country?

Cutti asked, phone camera already pointed at my face, because annoying me on video is her life's purpose.

I yawned so wide my jaw cracked.

Me: Yeeeesss

I replied with full joshh and a sleep-deprived expression. Hehe.

We had left Bengaluru on Feb 28th. Layover in Singapore, then Sydney, then Christchurch — more than 24 hours of flying, or maybe it just felt like that because we were chasing the east side of the globe and those guys are always ahead of us in time. Four of us. Me, my wife Pavithra (Cutti), my cousin Rithesh (Rinku), and Harini (Farini).

And the plan? Campervan. An RV. Our first ever. After Iceland, this was the one thing all four of us had been drooling over for months.

Day 1 · 01/03/2026

Christchurch → Fairlie

We landed in Christchurch around 3PM and were already running late. Britz, the company we had hired our campervan from, runs a free airport shuttle. We missed it. Obviously. What's the fun if we don't arrive late, eh? Every single time, lol.

Booked an Uber and literally ran into the Britz office.

Attendee: We are almost closing for the day, we cannot give you the van today

My heart dropped. If he said no, that's a full day gone — one day of a 14-day trip, plus a hotel we hadn't booked. We begged. Flight delays, long journey, first time in NZ, the whole sob story. He softened and agreed to hand over the keys. Only problem — everyone else had left for the day. No walkthrough. No demo. No instructions.

So we tossed a coin and took the wheel saying we'll figure it out.

Figure out WHAT exactly? We had absolutely no clue how to operate an RV. We knew how to steer and how to move it forward. That's it. How to refill fresh water, how to dump the waste, how the toilet works, where the storage boxes are, how the gas works — zero.

inner-me: Bro, this is a 4-berth house on wheels and you have never even parked a Innova properly

my inner-me reminded me as I climbed into the driver's seat.

It was raining. We didn't care. Pulled out towards Lake Tekapo with me driving and Rinku in the passenger seat reading the manual with such intensity that I'm fairly sure he'd have cleared every single engineering subject in one attempt if he had ever read like that in college, lol.

Campsites in NZ come in two flavours. Powered ones — mostly private, expensive, but you get shared kitchen, washrooms, hot showers. And unpowered ones — dirt cheap or completely free, like DOC campsites and freedom camping spots, usually parked right on a lakeside with a view that'll make you forget what a washroom even is.

The only thing they told us at the counter was this: look for plug-in campsites, the battery might need charging.

Why do I need a shared kitchen when I'm literally driving a full kitchen, I thought.

We stopped at Fairlie campsite, plugged in to charge, and by then it was almost evening. Cooked dinner, poked around the vehicle opening every cupboard like curious monkeys.

Temperature had dropped to 4°C. It was bloody cold. We just cuddled into those tiny cute beds and slept.

Last trip of the year with Rinku and Farini before they move to the US. That's what made this one heavier than any other. Until next time — Mā te wā. 🥝

interview_context.content: Hey! I'm so excited to hear about your trip. Tell me — where did you go, for how many days, and who came with you?
I went to new zealand March 1st to March 14th 2026

New Zealand for two whole weeks — amazing! Okay, quick math: that's 14 days (March 1st to 14th). Now tell me, who came along with you on this trip? Give me their full names, how you know them, and one thing that defines them!

I went with my Wife Pavithra Kala MP whom I call cutti, Rithesh Katta as Rinku my cousin and Harini RR as Farini
you can check my other blogs for their names and how based on situations we address each of them

Got it — Pavithra (cutti), Rithesh/Rinku (cousin), and Harini/Farini — love the nicknames! Before we dive into Day 1, give me one defining trait or quirk for each of them on this trip — like is Rinku the planner, is Farini the foodie who'd kill for kunafa, that kind of thing?
yes, you're right

Haha, love the confidence, but I need the specifics for each one! So — what's Pavithra's (cutti's) defining quirk on this trip? And separately, what's Rinku's thing, and what's Farini's thing? (Like "Rinku is the obsessive planner" or "Farini will die without her coffee")
you can skip that, and continue to the blog

No problem, we'll let their personalities shine through the stories as we go! Got everything I need for the overview.

So — Day 1, March 1st, New Zealand begins! Where did you land, and what happened first? Any chaos at the airport, first impressions, or that classic "wait, what do we do now" moment?

Mattuuuu, are you excited to visit your favorite country? Cutti started to make a video and annoy me as I yawned
Yeeeesss, I replied with full joshh with a sleep-deprived expression, hehe

it was on Feb 28th we started from Bengaluru, we had a very long flight spanning more than 24 hours, or it was also due to the fact that we were travelling towards east of the globe and they are ahead

we had a layout in Singapore, Sydney and then to Christchurch NZ. We started our trip from North New Zeland as we wanted to drive campervan/RV
It was our first RV trip too, seriously excited, I think after Iceland, this was what something we were all looking forward for

March 1st

We reached Christchurch around 3PM and it was already very late by the time we arrived at Britz, the company from whom we hired the campervan. As usual, what’s the fun if we do not arrive late heh? Every time, lol

We missed airport shuttle the Britz had, so booked the Uber and ran to the Britz office, if they had closed we would have to waste a day 

“We are almost closing for the day, we cannot give you the van today”, the attendee told as we entered the office

We tried to convince as our flights were delayed, and he was ready to give, but since everyone had already left, there was no one to give a tour of campervan and instructions, but guess what? We tossed a coin and took a wheel saying we will figure it out

Had absolutely no clue to operate RV except that we know how to steer the wheels and move the vehicle, no idea on features, anything, like how to refill water, how to operate washrooms, storage boxes, etc

It was raining already, we just did not care, we of course, would figure it out, we started driving towards Lake Tekapo, Me driving, Rinku reading manuals so deep that he would have passed all his subjects in engineering if he had ever read that seriously, lol

We were just told one thing, look for plug-in campsites as the battery might need charge. The campsites are of two types, powered and unpowered campsites. Powered are mostly private and expensive, but it will have shared kitchen, washroom, etc. 
The other ones, do not have power, the ones that are very cheap or some are free too like DOC campsites, freedom camping, etc but offers a great nature view like usually it will be on the lake side.

Why need a shared kitchen when we have hired a full fledged RV where we can cook, and do whatever we need to

Drive to Fairlie campsite, plugged into charge, it was almost eve by then, we had stopped for cooking dinner, exploring vehicle a bit.

The temp had dropped to 4 by then and it was extremely cold,  we just cuddled to sleep in tiny cute beds we had

This is such a perfect chaotic start — tossing a coin to just DRIVE an RV you have zero clue about, in the rain, is incredible. A few things I need to fill in Day 1:

1. What was going through your head (inner me moment) right when you grabbed the wheel with no instructions — were you secretly panicking?
2. What did you actually cook/eat that first night in the van, and how did that first cooking attempt go?
3. Any price shock — like how much was the Uber, or the campsite fee at Fairlie?

I was kinda anxious when I took the wheel, it was ny first time driving RV and it is big 4 seater btw

I do not remember what we cooked/ate, also, campsite fee was kinda expensive, not remember much, let us go to day 2

Got it, anxious first-time big RV driver in the rain — great visual! That's enough for Day 1, let's roll into Day 2.

What happened after Fairlie? Where'd you head next, and what was the big moment of the day?

You knew right how would it be on the first day of your trip, full excitement, full hopes and we also totally excited to start our day.

We thought before we take a wheel, we will figure out the campervan features, we checked out gas, how to refill water, how to read battery percentage and one thing we realised is the campervan comes with auto-recharge while we drive, so we wanted to see if we would really need paid campsite again for charging or not

It was time to open Kiran Sandwichwala’s signature breakfast - Lemon Semiya. We had yet to shop groceries, breads, eggs and milk, so it was a light breakfast and we took a wheel to Lake Tekapo, the first place every traveller visits to in South NZ

The temp was somewhat moderate and is it really a lake? It spans like 25-30kms

Lake tekapo, is an alpine lake, a lake something that sits on the mountain or alpine ranges, it was way too beautiful than we had imagined to be, we took a leisure stroll immersing ourselves in the nature. There was an picturesque bench too, got some candids there

Most of the lakes in NZ are turquoise blue, because most of them are fed from rivers flowed from the glacier. If there is a huge flow of water, then it will be usually in greenish color because of tiny sand granules being moved along the water, otherwise its turquoise blue, because once the sediment settles down, the water get that bluish color

Ritheshhh, what about lupins? Where is it? - Fariniiii chimed in with excitement 
How would I know? It was supposed to be here in the lakefront - He gave out the blunt reply like always

This time we had not really gotten time to plan TBH, since we did not have to worry about stays, etc because of campervan, we let the trip go more of impromptu. 

Anyways, we could not find any lupins, there was a good church at eye sight distance, Church of the Good Shepherd, only Rinku & Farinii went near to take some pictures, me and Cutti were just chilling on the lake side

We had to visit Tasman glacier view point, so we started driving alongside the Lake Pukaki, another turquoise blue lake, another woah moment 😛

On the way we visited lavender farm that lacked lavenders 😛they had just harvested all the flowers, all we got to see was plants, grabbed on lavender flavioured ice-cream and continued our journey

We drove across the beautiful landscapes of NZ which every reel on instagram shows off, the season we went was not much of a great landscape time, it is kinda dry season, like march in new zealand is end of summer almost, so mountains and all are dry.

Do you have a question why we still went in that season? Well, we chose NZ because of adventure activities and campervan experience, we had a good landscape hunt in Iceland, haha

I think was already around 5PM and we parked our campervan in parking spot and started walking towards the trail to reach tasman glacier view point.

It was a short hike, like 20 mins one way, around 1.5 kms, On the way we can see some blue lakes formed by the glacier of the alpine ranges and the view point has some crazy view with the lake infront and the tasman glacier behind, it is lke minimum effort max pleasure kinda thing 

We had some good banters at the view point, there were nobody except us. It was 7pm by then and we took some cool pictures, and we started back to the parking.

Daylights in NZ are longer, like you get 13-14 hours of daylight, so you can enjoy your evenings a lot. Drove to lake pukaki free campsite, it welcomed us with dark sky, 100s of campervans, millions of stars, we cooked some hot hot rasam, served ourselves with rice and yoghurt

Cherry on the cake? We got some cool video memory while we had this moment
Had dinner under the night full moon sky and stars 
Cozy sleep

Lupins that ghosted you, lavender farms with no lavenders, and dinner under a full moon at a free campsite — what a day. That line "minimum effort max pleasure" is gold.

One quick thing before we move on — any prices or costs stand out from today? Like the ice-cream, or was the free campsite actually totally free with no surprises?

Now, tell me about Day 3 — where'd you head next?

not really, free campsite is actually free with no surprises but there were no washrooms there, so.we had planned to visit Twizel there the next day

Also, washrooms or public toilets in nz are super clean except the dry ones which is mostly on the lake sides free campsites, but we never explored any on that day at lake pukaki campsite, because we used it in tasman glacier viewpoint and then used campervan's washroom

Good to know — clean toilets but no washrooms at free campsites, smart planning using the campervan's own loo. Noted!

Alright, Day 3 — tell me what happened when you drove to Twizel and beyond. Any new places, funny moments, food, or mishaps?

Early morning ride to hooker valley track at 4 am 
Orange hues on mt cook 
Came back to campsite and cooked some food 
Drove to twizel 
Swimming pool and hot shower after 3 days. 
Refilled water to camper van and cooked lunch. 
Fueled and drove to Queenstown. 
On the way stopped at lindis pass. Beautiful dry mountains with a scenic route in between 
Fergburger pick up and search for campsite 
Found one at 12 mile delta and had burger beer and slept 
Star gazing and eclipse - blood moon

Whoa, a 4am hike AND a blood moon eclipse in the same day — that's a packed one! Let's zoom into a couple of moments:

1. That 4am Hooker Valley Track start — brutal wake-up right? What was going through your head getting up that early, and was the orange sunrise on Mt Cook worth it?
2. Fergburger — notorious for its queues. Did you wait long, what'd you order, and was it worth the hype?
3. The blood moon eclipse at 12 Mile Delta sounds incredible — any reactions or quotes from the group when you saw it?

We had to get up early around 4am and drive as we were an hour away from Mt Cook, fortunately without tantrums of our wives, we left almost on the mark.

We packed ourselves with layers of fleece and jackets, we started the hooker valley track. It is almost 5kms. It is kinda Easy, utilizing gravel paths and boardwalks with three large suspension swing bridges

We started a bit late than what we thought of, around 6:15, the snowcapped mountain view ahead of us was luring us to start the walk, as we walked the trial, the sunrise started and we caught a good sight of golden hour, the orange hues spread our the alpine range, As we went along the hike, we saw hooker river and miller river

Hooker River: This is the main, rushing alpine river that flows through the length of the valley. You will walk right alongside it and cross directly over it three separate times via the trail's iconic swinging suspension bridges (the Lower Hooker, Hooker Bluff, and Upper Hooker bridges). The river is famous for its distinct, milky light-blue or grey colour, which comes from fine rock particles known as "glacial flour" suspended in the water. 
Mueller River / Stream: Near the very beginning of the hike, the first suspension bridge crosses the roaring waters right where Mueller Lake feeds out. The trail bridges the gap where the flow from the glacier lakes merges into the main valley path. 

The last bridge was under construction, so we could not go till the actual peak, we reached the last one and soaked ourselves in warming sunlight and view of the hooker river and alpine ranges. Was it worth? Of course, you ask a mountain lover, he says 1000% percent worth it, hahah

We reached back to the parking, cooked some eggs, peeled oranges, cooked breakfast and savoured it watching the snowcapped mountains 

What’s next? Take bath man, my inner me mocked at as it was 3 days since I had taken a bath, lol

We drove to Twizel, an amazing small cute town, we used public restrooms and then what? We went to swim in Twizel community pool and also took bath. Such a refreshing feeling it was to swim and float and then to take a hot water bath. 

There was a place to refill the water and dump the waste as well, we finished campervan rituals, lol sounds fun, but to do it, it is not.

We fueled and Our next stop was, the famous queenstown, enroute, the route was so scenic despite being dry, we passed across a lindis pass and stopped by the view point.

All through the drive, cutti was sleeping and I had taken some pics in Lindis Pass. 
“Why you did not wake me up?”, She questioned us
‘We did, but you were so much in deep sleep, you said you will not come and we can go enjoy the view”, I said
Me Farini and Rinku had discussed we will play with her for sometime, thankfully we were all on the same page :-P

Somehow she figured out later that we did not actually wake her up, and it was too sunny, a complete weather shift compared to the last two days.

I had taken a good nap after Lindis Pass, and Rinku did the driving till Queenstown and our first stop was Ferg Burger, how did we find this? We have our master finder for these things, Ms Fariniii, the one who knows everything about food and cafes wherever we go.

It was long line to grab one big burger, thanks to my sleep, I was still kicked into sleep, while they all went and bought me one good burger for the meal

We had not planned for campsite, after searching couple of them in queenstown, everything was full, we drove a bit far to 12 mile delta and had burger, beer and slept 

Perk of driving to 12 mile delta campsite? Man it was blood moon day and we witnessed it. Millions of stars with the blood moon made a perfect picturesque . it was the only total lunar eclipse of 2026 and marked the last blood moon visible worldwide until late 2028. 

We wrapped our day. It was our time to sleep on the bigger bed 😛

That prank on Cutti pretending to wake her up is SO relatable — "we did, but you were in deep sleep" 😂 And catching the only blood moon of 2026 by pure luck of a full campsite? Incredible payoff.

Alright, Day 4 — what happened in Queenstown and beyond? Any adventure activities, since you mentioned that's a big reason you picked NZ?

Woke up to a beautiful sunrise by the Wilson bay formed by lake wakatipu, that is where the 12 mile delta campsite was. We had a shotover jet at 10:30 AM, so we had to be there early to not miss out due to delays that had happened in silfra fissure in iceland.

I took a small stroll towards the lake, stretched out. Freshened up and spread the tables, cut the oranges and cooked the breakfast and kick started our adventure day

It was fully packed with bunch of adrenaline activities, we first went to shotover jet, at first, it seemed like a normal jet, but hold your horses, that 360 degree spin, omg

“How would it be to be a jet boat driver?” I thought
“Yeah, seems like a stable job compared to AI in IT” my inner me stated a blunt fact

I told my wife that I wanted to be a jet boat driver and settle down in Queenstown, to which she dismissed my feelings as if I was not serious
Well, which is most of the times 😛



We had a good ride, crazy spins, it was seriously so awesome and one of the kind. It is named shotover jet as the activity is done on the shotover river.

We then headed to kawarau swing and wanted to bungee too, but did not get the slots, I and Cutti did couple swing, whereas Rinku did solo. 
Fariniii is afraid of activities and she did not do 

I was kinda afraid too while doing the swing, you can notice it, lol. I am afraid of heights, but still I do it always. The only way to get rid of fear is to keep doing it more n more.

As the confusion grew over my mind to do Bungee in Kawarau or in Nevis? Rinku challenged me to do it in Nevis. Nevis is 143m while Kawarau is just 43. I have done 83 mts in Rishikesh and why to do less now

While I was still battling with courage, desire, fear and challenge, Rinku wanted to do cliff jump and we drove to Little Thailand. Man, that was serious thing, there was no one at the spot and we did not know if it is a right place. Just then a localite and his friend came out jumping, then we were like fine, this is the spot. Me n Rinku started hiking down, we have to hike down a bit for about 100 meters and then there is a dive spot.

At first, I thought I will try, never tried without a life jacket, but this was a real deal, no safety, no life jacket, nobody to pull you up if you have drowned, a real shit

Rinku saw the depth, it was around 45 ft for sure, he gasped his breath, and sat down a min. 
“Okay, boy, this is definitely not yours”, my inner me warned and yes, did not wanted to risk without anyone helping out there. Just when I am still processing, rinku jumped. Omg what a feeling it was for him. He came up so happy. 

Do you know something, he infact jumped from a little top than where he was supposed to, lil. He figured out the diving spot while coming up, there was another clean section to stand and jump.

Anyways, we were all so contended, many more adventures to go, we had a good fish, monk and blue cod and then some pretty Gelato at Ferg

It was almost eve and girls were curious about the Hydroattach, a semi submarine kind of a ride that goes inside the water, it seemed cool, for them and not for the boys 😛
Apparently, slot was not there, we headed to luge

6 rounds of crazy luge with arrow and dart circuits was something that bought the inner child outside, what a fun it was, Luge is a small cart where you can sit inside control the speed of driving along the two tracks, the found round was decent, from second, we all raced non stop and did some cool rides

We had to to MIlford the next day, so we thought we will do the other activities while coming back, so we headed over to Lumsden camping site en route Milford Sound

That cliff jump moment is intense — Rinku just going for it while you held back, then finding out he misjudged the spot afterward. Great tension there!

Quick follow-up: Did you end up doing the bungee at all (Nevis or Kawarau), or did you let that one go? And any prices that stood out today — like cost of the Shotover Jet, luge rounds, or that fish & blue cod meal?

all the adventure activities costed us a fortune, a couple swing was 240  NZD per person, shotover jet and luge was around 16K INR per person

and yeah, I did Nevis later, why would I back out huh? hehe

Ha! Knew you wouldn't back out of Nevis — respect. We'll catch that story when it happens chronologically.

Okay, 240 NZD for the couple swing and ~16K INR each for Shotover/Luge — adventure really does cost a fortune in Queenstown! Noted.

Day 5 — tell me about the drive to Milford Sound. What happened?
while mentioning prices, convert it to inr and mention

Got it, I'll make sure to convert all those NZD prices to INR when writing the blog!

Now, Day 5 — tell me about the drive to Milford Sound. What happened along the way, and what was Milford Sound itself like?

We booked last slot at Milford at 3:30, we left leisurely at lumsden, it was a good place and we had everything in same camp ground, water refill, waste dumping, etc

So we did all campervan chores and left to Milford. 
Then drove towards to Milford via lake te anau, it was beautiful and as usual we had left late, we decided to come back later, we did not have plans for later today as did not know where to halt, lol, I told you right, we are full impromptu sometimes


The drive was different than what we did before, this time it was full of dense forest, kinda western ghats feeling. The south western part of NZ is mostly wet and filled with dense forest and fordlands while the central and north western is filled with glaciers and alpine ranges


We hoarded the boat and best sight it was, As we sailed, the captain explained the history of milford and some geography about it. 
Also, there are some mountains there has unique compositions, they say it might also contain gold. Not sure, Since rain wasn’t there, the scenic was not like how we see in social media, but still it was very beautiful, the giant mountains standing out, the waterfalls especially Lady Bowne and Stirling falls in some of them was worth the sight. 

Milford was more of a fjord rather than a sound. A fjord is something that is formed by glaciers carving through the rocks, a sound is something that is formed by rivers carving out, though milford seem like a sound now, if we go back in history, it is due to glaciers. 

After the boating, we drove back to Lumsden, on the way stopped at Te Anau for sunset and some chill time. It got pretty dark soon today and we could not spend a lot of time at the lake side.


It was Kinda long day but worth it. 
Late dinner followed by good sleep without alarms for next day, lol
It was extremely windy that day and were thinking if the camepervan falls apart, lol
We and our crazy thoughts

Haha, "thinking if the campervan falls apart" in the wind — the crazy thoughts of an exhausted traveler! Love that you got to chill at Te Anau without an alarm waiting the next morning.

Day 6 — what's next on the itinerary? Any new activities or places?

How fun it would be to have a slow morning, with zero plans in mind and all we need to think about is where to take bath, lol

We finished all campervan no-fun rituals and went to swim. There was a community pool nearby, we paid at the shop opposite to campsite and took a stroll in the neighborhood to reach the community pool

In NZ, usually community pools, will have hot showers and best way to shower, quite expensive like 3-5 nzd per person, but still it is fine. Campervan does not reduce any of your expenses that you would spend on traditional hotels, taxis or self rental cars, it is just that it gives you a complete freedom camping on those lakesides and beautiful spots. And a different feel, but better be careful, it is extremely additive, atleast for me, it was

It adds a lot of tasks on your plate, like self-cooking, self-cleaning vehicle,etc but that’s the fun. 

We all sat down to figure out what to do and we decided, will go queensland and probably do bungee, still I am not sure, and even Cutti, was quite hesitant. 

While Rinku took the wheel, I just grabbed my credit card and booked the slot. No seeing and all after reaching queenstown, I will definitely not back out if I pay for it, lol. Paisa vasoool guy I am 😛

Cutti still was hesitant, anyways she said she will do kawarau, so we decided, I will report to AJ Hackett office since I had to take their shuttle, while Rinku and Farini will drive cutti to Kawarau where she can do.

I took the shuttle and fully nervous, jumping from 441ft, 143m is no easy for someone who is altophobic like me. Yet gathered courage, played some music and then reached the place. A long iron bridge suspended over two alps and in mid there is a big box, where the jumper usually jumps from. Forget about seeing the view from that box, I am shit scared to see the entire setup from the edge of the mountain itself.

Somehow got into the trolley carrying us into the box from the mountain edge, I was the 3rd person. One thing I was confident was, no matter how afraid I am, I will still do, because I have paid for it, lol

All geared up, stood on the edge, I still freaking do not remember how did I fall, I opened my eyes in between, it was soo smooth and satisfying. Once jump, you bounce back a bit and then fall again, it was soo smooth compared to rishikesh. After the second jump, there was rope, I should pull, if I do, the bungee cord snaps to the harness near the stomach, so I can be in sitting position and enjoy the view 

“Fyck yeashhhh, I finally did it”, I was so overjoyed at that moment, capturing fear is something crazy feeling.

So happy, I got into the bus and called them that I finally did it and asked about Cutti’s jump
Guess what? They took sweet time for shopping souvenirs at DF Souviniers and gave some lame reason that the last slot to book was already over by the time they enquired. I got to know only after I called them back on the way back.

I got so pissed, anyways, it is her first jump, so we decided, we will see tomorrow once and chilled on boundary street park. We thankfully got the free parking in boundary street, the evenings in queenstown was so amazing, the pinkish golden hour, with families playing sport in the park was something that made us question the busy life we live in cosmopolitan. 

What about celebrations for the jump? Well, had good beer and another ferg burger and wrapped up the day.

"No seeing and all after reaching Queenstown, I will definitely not back out if I pay for it" — that's such a perfectly human strategy! And booking it blind via credit card while Rinku drove is great. The Nevis jump description is intense — "Fyck yeashhhh, I finally did it" is exactly the raw dialogue this blog needs.

Also lol at them going souvenir shopping and missing Cutti's slot — bet that conversation was fun when you found out!

So Day 6 wrapped with beer, Fergburger, and golden hour at Boundary Street. Day 7 — what happened next? Did Cutti finally get her Kawarau jump in?
Oh yeah, we also slept looking forward to the next day as it was sky diving, all of our first sky dive except Rinku's

Oh, sky diving! That's huge — and Rinku's already a pro while the rest of you are first-timers. Tell me everything about Day 7 — how'd the skydive go, did Cutti get her Kawarau jump too, and what was going through your heads before jumping out of a plane?

It was a skydive day, yaaay. We were excited so much; we had a morning slot at 10:30, so we freshened up and cooked breakfast and left to Wanaka

We went to SkyDive Wanaka NZ which is the company we had booked skydive, we were prepped with instructions and suited up, guess what
“Hey, we have to push your booking as there clouds and no visibility”, the guide said

They did not give us any hopes of when they might do it again, we could opt for refund or wait as long as we want or reschedule too. We rescheduled it to 2:30 and drove to Community Centre where there was a shower and we could freshen up

We freshened up and arrived an hour before just to be double sure and yeah, we were suited up again after the wait.

So tensed and also thrilled, and “I am not going first”, Fariniii said and he told diver to jump with her at the last

As usual, Rinku went first, me second, third cutti and last Fariniiii.

My first sky dive, I was so lost in the view, the diver is tappin on my shoulder, if he taps, we can spread our arms and enjoy the view for photograph. I was so lost, he kept tapping and I did not realise until the end, lol

Somehow got some pics and we got a good view of wanaka and hawai
 Lake, and landing? It was sooo smoooth . Best experience ever, Absolutely loved it.

What’s next? As we had to drive further up the north now, we decided we will drive via Queenstown and let Cutti do her bungy today. We had only 40 mins gap, and evening slot was booked for hydro attack. 

“Mattu, we will do in Rishikesh, it is fine”, she tried to push it today as well. I said, rishikesh also we will do no, we will do here

I called up AJ Hackett, they said no slots, I decided to drive by and check out there at counter in the site. Ran to the booking and asked her for a slot, thankfully, we got one. While she went to change, I requested to send her quick soon after their lunch break as we had another activity, the bookie agreed and cutti was third on the row to jump.

I was on the viewing deck thinking this money is gone, because, I was honestly not sure she was gonna make it.

She stood on the board, there she goes, a perfect bungee leap. I screamed yaaaay and I was so happy and proud of my brave girl. She definitely is beyond my expectations huh? Lol

I was so happy, collected her complimentary t-shirt and went to hydroattack, but was cancelled due to high tides. 

We headed towards North East of South Island, which is glacier route. Our next stop was Franz Joseph. It was an 5 hour ride, we did not wanted to rush, so we decided to camp in Bendigo Campsite which is on the Clutha River which was just an hour from there. 

We reached there by 7pm around, a perfect sunset time, put out the table and chairs and had one of the best quality time out there. Me and cutti took a small stroll towards Clutha river and cherished the whole evening. 

“Mattu, swim with dolphins”, Cutti said as we had one crazy dolphin swim at Kaikora
Me and Rinku looked in despair; just when we finished all the unplanned ones we are all equally excited to do this too. 

But we were not sure as we were kinda confused to go to whrariki or skip it as it’s gonna be a long ride. 

“Macha, let’s do. We will just drive a bit more each day and do the circuit”, I suggested and of course why would the group say no. Despite this idea, we never bothered to book that, lol
As usual we and our last minute bookings.

What a rollercoaster of a day — cloud delays, first skydives, Cutti FINALLY conquering her bungee fear ("this money is gone" 😂), and then capping it off with a gorgeous sunset at Bendigo campsite. "She definitely is beyond my expectations" is such a sweet line.

Also love that you added a whole new plan (dolphin swim at Kaikoura) without actually booking anything — very on-brand for this trip, haha.

Day 8 — tell me what happened as you continued toward Franz Joseph and the glacier route!

Since washrooms there were dry toilets, we did not wanted to freshen up there, so started our day a bit early and we drove to Wanaka lake, parked our campervan, got
What a peaceful life, I thought, looking at the some people, they had gotten their boats and was sailing on the lake

Few parents with kids had let the kids play out there, how cool it is to get up visit a lake and having fun, I miss them in cities like where we live. I mean NZ is such a cool balanced country in terms of quality of life, of course, if you’re someone who wants social life, that is not the one.

And some Kids doing the kayak and morning walks by localities emphasised life skills and health over anything 

“I wanna be in Wanaka”, I said with josh
“Yeah, you wanna be a boat driver in shotover jet, you wanna be in queenstown, now in wanaka, what all you want to be? Have some clarity”, Farinii mocked at me
Heh

And you might be wondering, how many times we go to queenstown, wanaka over and over? Well, that’s what impromptu planning gives you, no fixed itinerary, keep flexible, come back with no regrets. 
Of course, we could have booked activities well in advance and planned it up, well, it is okay, it was run rather this way. I love our partners Rinku and Farini as we all sail with same mindset and peace with it, Cheers

We left after an hour or so, on the way first stop Lake hawai
 Viewpoint, the very same like that I had admired in skydive, well, it was too sunny, just glanced a view and started again.

We had plenty of places today, enroute to franz joseph, there are some tons of falls, off beat places, creeks.

First stop was Blue pools dip, why not take a dip here? My inner me said and also fresh clear glacier water
Me n Rinku went a little head than the wives who walked lika tortoise, water was freezing cold and biting. I slowly got into the water, but could not stay longer than a min, it was that freaking cold.

I took a short break and then went in again, never got into one that was this cold, so felt great and energised, we took some pictures there, but flies are huge issues in NZ, it started to irk us a alot, so we left the place

Then came Wilson creek, Farinii n RInku did not come, Me n Cutti went in, but again water was shit cold, Cutti, almost gave up until I told her to take a breath and come again. To see the creek, we had to go into the water which was above the ankle depth, since it was extremly cold, the numbness and biting was refraining her not to come. Thanks for the blue pools dip I had, I was kinda used to it

well what’s creek? A creek is narrow piece of water entering into land from sea 

That was google def but the creeks here were diff, the Wilson creek had a huge rock cut open like a cave and a water was following through it. 
“Go climb that rock and take a picture” my inner me finally said and I got one, lol 

Next was fantail falls and Thunder Creek, was exhausted we just saw that from distant and back on the wheel. 

By then we had to unload the waste water and refill with a fresh one, we got one at Haast en route franz Joseph. 

I was done driving for the day and slept at the back while Rinku drove to Paringa Campsite closer to franz Joseph and wrapped our day with the dreams of flying over the glacier the next day and first helicopter ride of mine, haha

"You wanna be a boat driver, now in Wanaka, what all you want to be? Have some clarity" — Farini really keeping you grounded, haha! And that progression from freezing at Blue Pools to being "kinda used to it" by Wilson Creek is such a relatable cold-water battle.

Day 9 — first helicopter ride over the glacier at Franz Joseph! How'd that go? Were you nervous, and what was the view like?

Got up early and Rinku drove to lake matheson and did circuit for sunrise, 

“Wow, whatta perfect reflection”, i said to myself the lake Matheson is a circuit, with two lakes and both the lakes has perfect mirror reflection of the nature around it. It has got some eels which are mostly hunted by Māori tribe and they serves this eel as meal for their cultural festivals. Otherwise it’s difficult to even hunt for others. People can’t get into the lake as well 
Okay, hurry up, we are getting late for the glacier ride, Rinku said and we had to reach there by 10:30
We were all so excited, we finished up ore checks and formalities and boarded the chopper. 
The ride went over  the fox glacier and captain explained why it was called as fox, it’s because of the the glacier end that looks like the fox tail,
We had a landing over the glacier, as usual fun time for us, we grabbed some fresh snow and threw over each other. I and Rinku tasted some ice too, lol  
We got some really cool pictures and got back to franz Joseph. We were all tired, put some break for the quick lunch and straight to hokitika George. 

Creek, Gorge what’s all this our of dictionary words, my inner me was struggling to understand 
A Gorge is a valley between two steepy sloppy mountains with a water flowing in between. 
Hokitika was similar to blue pools but it was just green and more calmer I felt. Didn’t bother much to get into the water, we just sat there and forgot all worries for a while and enjoyed the view until sandflies troubled us to leave :-P 
We had another long journey today, the next day was wharaRiki beach, we tried to cover a lot this time despite having no plan, all we had to do was drive a bit more everyday. We had no issues and also, what else we have a motor home for? 
We had a beautiful sunset at punaikaki pancakes. A huge boulder inPunaikaki is named like that because of the pancake shape formed by the rocks, those aren’t just rocks, those are basically the limestone Rock formations because of the calcium from the dead bones of fish and marine life. It was so deep into the sea but now it’s 30-40 ft above sea level, imagine what global warming has made nowadays. 

To wharariki it was another 6 hour drive, so we decide to halt atwai iti domain campsite which is like 2 hours from wharariki and 4 hours from punaikaki.
“Macha you drive now and I will drive in the morning”, Rinku said as he knows I won’t get up on time in the morning. 
Played some songs, often listening to Cutti’s snoring, lol 
She was supposed to give me company but chose to snore
Finally we arrived at campsite but it was not like other sites, just a plain empty ground, felt like a haunted place but was too tired to even give a duck. Put my bed under and just crashed.

Throwing snow at each other on a glacier landing — what a core memory! And "played some songs, often listening to Cutti's snoring" while driving through the night to a spooky empty campsite is such a vivid closer for the day.

Day 10 — tell me about reaching Wharariki Beach! Did you end up booking that dolphin swim, or any other adventures along the way?

I had a dream that someone is shaking me so hard to wake me up, but apparently it was not the dream, Rinku shaking me to wake me up. He got up early and drove to Wharariki, lol

It was around 8am by then, we freshened up in parking, made some breakfast and decked up, It has a short hike from parking to the beach, that’s what they said :-P, but it did not feel short despite it being just 1km 

After the hike, we had to go another few hundred meters on the sand to reach the beach shore, the sand had formed dunes due to regular heavy winds and it was very tiresome to walk on that due to feet going inside and us putting additional effort to get it back and place next step

“Ah, pristine white sand beach, like any other country”, my inner me amused me as we reached the shore.

Whaririki is famous for windows lock screen image, beach was beautiful, yet too sunny to even enjoy its beauty.
It had crazy dramatic rock formations, more dramatic than Farinii when she convinces us for going to some cool cafe 😛
We tried to replicate Windows' lock screen, but thanks to our no-skill photography, where we could not figure out how that photographer really took it from what angle. We got some good shots though, chilled for a while and I said, “Come on, let us go for a spa day”

You know right? Every trip of ours usually ends with a cool bath, spa, etc. 
As we walked back, the spa was very close by, apparently I was being questioned that why Rinku, Farini, Cutti nobody saw it when they checked google. Yet they trusted me with full confidence only when I started to navigate from there, I realised I was seeing the spa that was in Rotorua, Dammit
Anyways since now we were sure of going to Kaikora, we decided we shall book Swim with dolphins. We and our last minute never ending plans, 

But luck on this day wasn’t on our side, all slots were sold out at Kaikora Dolphin, it’s a famous company. There was another one but didn’t had that great reviews. But still good 

Finally they put us on waiting list in case someone cancels their slot, we can have one, we all hoped for that and started driving in case, if we did not get this, we can go with other agency

We started driving towards the east coast to reach kaikora. En route stopped at motukeka and took hot shower. 

While we were on the run, “Stop the music”, Rinku said as he got a call from unknown number; he spoke seriously while we were all thinking what happened. 

““Yes yes, we for slot for dolphin swim on 8:30”, he was jumping, haha 


It was dusk by then, and we started driving toward the heavy ghat section; it was past 11 pm, and I was driving while Rinku had fallen asleep in the bed above the driver's seat. I was in around 70kmph and started seeing the police trailing me with the lights on, since I thought they are just patrolling, after a min, started to hear the siren too, I parked the campervan on the side of the road and a cute cop walked in, I am not bluffing, she was really cute man.

“Sir, can I see your license?”, she asked, after seeing all documents, she said I am speeding, the limit is 50kmps in town limits.
I said sorry and she entered details in her phone, took photo and said to follow the speed limit sign boards and was good enough to let us go without a fine

She wasn’t just cute, but also polite and respectable and good enough to let us go


Oh btw, she told I would be fined next time if I drive with passenger sleeping in campervan while vehicle is on the move. I did not know this, damn we should have reached early and gotten all this instructions when we got campervan.

Anyways, Rinku and Farini sat down with seat belt on for sometime and then back to bed after we left town limits. Finally it was 1am when we reached Kaikora campsite, I crashed in like always with a sweet dream of dolphins swim

Oh my god, accidentally navigating to a spa in Rotorua instead of nearby, AND getting pulled over by a cute, polite cop who let you off — what a day of plot twists! Getting that waitlist call for dolphins while driving was such perfect timing too.

Day 11 — the dolphin swim at Kaikoura! How'd it go? Were you nervous getting in the water, and what was the experience actually like?

Guess what? Rinku got up at 8 and he has missed his alarm, thank god we were close by to the Dolphin swim agency centre where we had to report, it was like 10 mins. We all woke up and quick 2 mins freshen up  & rushed towards the reporting location.

While me and Rinku went in to check in and do formalities, Farini and Cutti prepared the bread and hummus. We had it while taking the training.

After a quick brief up on wet suit handling, swim, etiquettes of interacting with dolhon, we headed into sea towards south of pacific.

We all got masked up and geared, ready for the first honk by captain, and swoosh, we all jumped into the water with our masks on.

Omg, seriously, whattta feeling, 100s of dolphins just passes by under you, sometimes you end up touching them without even wanting to. I really run out of words to express the feeling. We also saw some cool dolphins breaching meaning jumping out of water. And, also spinner, which leap into the air and spin around multiple times before landing.

Once the second honk, we need to enter back to boat and then they will wait for another pod where we can jump in again and swim with them. We can do it for 5 times, totally Paisaaa Vasoool. Really one of the kind. 


We were shit tired by then, we had not had proper breakfast, drove to south bay campsite for breakfast and lunch. Almost end of our South NZ trip, we drove to pak n save, shopped tim tams and chocolates and headed to campsite near the beach in Christchuch and halted

Swimming with 100s of dolphins and getting "Paisa Vasool" out of it five times over — incredible way to almost wrap up South Island! And the Tim Tam shopping run feels like the perfect "we're nearly done" beat.

So this is near the end of the South Island leg — are you handing back the campervan in Christchurch next, or is there more to Day 11/12? And since you started this trip wanting to explore North NZ with the RV too — walk me through what's left: the Christchurch return and the move north?

One last day at Christchurch, planned lot of things to explore but missed everything, why? Damnnn campervan rituals, we had to clean the van and clear out all waste before returning, if we had taken a special package with extra 250 nzd or something, we could have returned as it is without cleaning, refuel of gas or petrol or anything, who knew we would end up spending almost 230 nzd on gas, fuel refilling alone

It took us almost an hour and half to clean, and then fill up cooking gas and petrol, made one last stop at nearby DS Souviniers to take a kiwi for our home.


We handed ove the campervan and flew to Auckland.

We switched to car this time, as it was just two day in North NZ, rav4 Toyota and drove towards waitomo caves for the next day boating tour.

I would not suggest this as we wasted one full day for campervan duties and flight. Rather take a campervan at Auckland, drive down towards south and use ferry to cross the north - south. We had anyway planned to whrariki and kaikora which is on extreme north of south NZ, if you’re planning same, start from north and come to south and handover campervan in Christchuch, you can do it. 

We were not sure of Kaikora or entering north region right, so we thought driving one day in campervan is waste considering effort, fuel costs, etc. But now I feel driving is better than having to wait like a dumb in airport for a short transfers.

Good tip for future travelers — that logistics lesson about campervan vs flight transfer is gold for the Tips section!

So you've landed in Auckland, picked up the RAV4, and are heading to Waitomo Caves. Is this your final day (Day 12) before wrapping up the trip, or do you have more days left? Tell me about the Waitomo boating tour — what happened there, and how does the trip end?

We were almost end of our NZ trip, finished all adventures, yet another exciting moment of meeting then Cutti’s friend - Nannaiah, now he is all our friend, haha

We woke up a bit early from our cozy airbnb, cooked some food and it was all about nanniah’s plan day, we thought will do waitomo caves and then do whatever he suggests as he stays in Hamilton. 

We drove waitomo, took a boat ride and wow, glow worms in the ceiling of limestone caves was a sight to behold. Limestone caves is shinier usually in nature, but glow worms adding its pure greenish glow to the dark caves is another beauty altogether.

We were instructed to keep our phones on silent to not disturb the space, we got blurry pictures and just when I was thinking why our Fariniii is not feeling hungry, she said “Let’s go for some place to eat no, I am already hungryy”, haha, timings match

We drove to rotorua, and visited Lime Cafe on the lakeside, a good stop for lunch. 
“Rotorua is the place where the first zorb was invented; you would love to try?”, Nanniah suggested

One more adventure? Why not
It was already late and the last zorb slot was at 4, so we hurried up, I made it to booking counter and got 5 tickets to Zorb

The Zorb has various trials; we can choose what we like. We chose the swirly zig-zag track to keep it more fun, and just when we were thinking to do what’s next? 

“Why not we go to the spa that I thought it is in wharariki? Anyway, it is in Rotorua right? “, I chimed in
“Hmmm, not a bad idea, let us go”, all jinxed 

Nanniah had other plans for the day, he would meet us next day, so he went to Hamilton and we went to Hells Gate

Hells Gate is NZ geothermal mud spa, again, we had to run, since we were running out of closing time, and guess what? We entered, paid, and they shut the counters, lol
We need to work on our timings for sure eh? Hehe

Mud spa has 3 sections, where your journey begins with a rejuvenating 20-minute soak in warm, mineral-rich volcanic mud that naturally exfoliates and detoxifies your skin. Next, you will rinse off and invigorate your circulation in a refreshing cool plunge or waterfall dip before transitioning into the soothing warmth of the naturally heated sulphur mineral pools to completely melt away muscle tension. 

The experience was unforgettable for 2 reasons, one, it was our first mud spa, second, damn, everyone skin started itching except Rinku’s where he fell sick instead

There was something off in that mud or suphur but idk, not gonna try again, damn.
After continuous run, got back to Airbnb by the redwood cottage Cooked biryani and rasam rice and slept.

Meeting Nanniah and him becoming "all our friend" is such a sweet addition, and that itchy mud spa mishap (with Rinku getting sick instead!) is a perfect "logistics gone wrong" beat for the blog.

Is this the final day of the trip, or is there one more day before you fly back? And if this is the last one — any final moment before departure you want to include?

We all woke up with a feeling of missing out being in NZ, all the thoughts of me being in Wanaka, Cutti n Farini wanting to be in Queenstown is all gonna just be another dream.

We had kept it as a leisure day, cooked one last semiya, sipped one last coffee in the BnB. We coordinated with Nanniah that we will meet at Blue pools Spring. 
Blue pools spring is A massive freshwater spring located near Putāruru, they say most of the NZ supplied from here, it was a trial walk across the spring. At the end it also has its history and how Maori tribes tried to protect the water, village, etc.

We were officially done sightseeing, so we took a short stop to Mc Laren lake grabbed some pizzas at Pizza Jack, crashed at the nearby park. Played uno cards, had long banters, joked about each other, took a quick power nap. Whatta day to end the trip

Also, we were not just the people who did this, so many new zealanders do camp in these public parks, do barbeque, grab beers and have fun. Truly balanced and quality time with family 

We drove across the city, grabbed Gelato, took a eve beach walk, and it was time to bid bye to NZ and Nanniah, 

From there, we drove to Auckland airport, enjoying the orange sunset hues of the sky. We bid by to Nanniah, dropped of cab and boarded the flight with heavy memories.
It was also harder than any other trip of ours because this was this years last trip with Rinku and Farini as they were moving to US in a month or two. 

So Until next time, Mā te wā (see ya next time)

What a bittersweet way to end — Uno cards in the park, pizza, gelato, and knowing it's the last trip with Rinku and Farini before they move. "Mā te wā" is such a lovely closer.

Okay, we've covered the whole journey! Let's wrap this up properly. A few final questions:

1. If you had to pick ONE single best moment of the entire 14 days, what would it be?
2. What's one thing you'd tell a friend NOT to do (a mistake or regret)?
3. Quick must-visit vs overrated/skip list — any places you'd tell someone to definitely see, and any that weren't worth it?

best moment? of course, driving ̉RV in an unknown land and Nevis jump, scary, yet something I am proud of doing it

Def not to opt out for a campervan cleaning package, lol

wanaka tree is overrated, indeed we skipped it, must visit is treks in Mt Cook, plz do if someone loves treks and ferg burger and monk cod in queenstown

Perfect, that's gold for the Tips and Must Visit sections!

Last thing — give me the quick city-to-city itinerary route for the blog (like Christchurch → Lake Tekapo → Twizel → ... → Auckland), just the path you took.

you build the city to city itinerry based on info you have and ensure you add website for britz, and all apps we used campermate and for fuel Gaspy which is very much used to figure out cheap fuel places and for esim, we used mobimatter
Got everything I need! Writing your blog now...

excerpt: "Mattuuuu, are you excited to visit your favorite country?" Cutti asked, phone camera already pointed at my face, because annoying me on video is her life's purpose.  I yawned so wide my jaw cracked.  "Yeeeesss," I replied with full joshh and a sleep-deprived expression. Hehe.  We had left Bengaluru

items: Do NOT skip the campervan cleaning package — this is my single biggest regret of the trip.
Britz offers a pre-paid package (around 250 NZD / ~₹13,000) where you just hand the van back as-is — no cleaning, no refuelling gas, nothing.

We skipped it to be smart, and spent 1.5 hours scrubbing a motorhome on our last day in Christchurch, plus almost 230 NZD (~₹12,000) on petrol and gas refills anyway, and missed the entire city. Smart, huh.
Reach the rental office on time — we got the van with zero instructions because we rolled in at closing.
We then spent 10 days learning things the hard way — including a cop telling us that passengers are not allowed to sleep in the bed while the campervan is moving.
We had NO idea that's a fineable offence — learn it from a manual, not from a police officer at 11PM.
Download CamperMate before you land (campsites, dump stations, water refill, toilets — this is your bible).
Download Gaspy — it shows you the cheapest fuel around you, and in NZ fuel prices swing a LOT between stations.
Download MobiMatter for the eSIM, and book the rental at britz.co.nz.
Free campsites are genuinely free — no hidden charges.
DOC sites and freedom camping spots gave us lakeside views that paid campsites could never.
Lake Pukaki free campsite — 100s of campervans, millions of stars, zero rupees.
Just know most free sites have dry toilets, so plan your "serious business" around proper towns.
Community pools are the hack for showers — 3–5 NZD per person (~₹150–250) and you get a swim AND a hot shower.
Twizel and Lumsden pools saved our souls after 3 days of not bathing.
A campervan will NOT save you money — let me kill this myth.
Between rental, fuel, gas, campsites and pool showers, it costs roughly what hotels + rental car would.
You pay for freedom, not savings — but god, that freedom is addictive. At least for me.
Plan your north-south direction properly — do NOT do what we did: campervan in the south, fly to Auckland, rent a car for the north.
We wasted an entire day on cleaning + airport waiting.
Instead: pick up the campervan in Auckland, drive south, take the ferry across, finish at Christchurch.
Especially if Wharariki and Kaikoura are on your list — they're at the top of the South Island anyway.
Book adventure activities in advance — we were full impromptu and it cost us.
Missed bungy slots on day 4, missed Hydro Attack twice, nearly missed the dolphin swim (got in only off a waitlist call).
Queenstown slots vanish fast.
Adventure in NZ costs a fortune, so pick your battles.
Couple swing at Kawarau — 240 NZD per person (~₹12,500); Shotover Jet and Luge — around ₹16,000 per person.
Nevis Bungy is 143m vs Kawarau's 43m — if you're doing one bungee in your life, do Nevis.
If you're scared of heights like me — still do Nevis.
Pay first, panic later — you will never back out once the money's gone. Paisa vasool psychology.
Overrated: The Wanaka Tree. It's a tree. In water. We skipped it with zero regret, you can too.
We went end of Feb–March, which is the tail of summer.
Mountains are dry and brown, not the lush green Instagram version.
Go for the adventure activities and the campervan life, not for landscapes — for landscapes, Iceland wins.
Upside: 13–14 hours of daylight, so your evenings are enormous.
Sandflies are the real villains of New Zealand — Blue Pools, Hokitika Gorge, Wilson Creek, they chased us out of every single beautiful spot.
Carry repellent. Seriously.
Hells Gate mud spa — maybe skip; three of us itched for hours and Rinku straight up fell sick.
Something in that sulphur mud wasn't our thing — your mileage may vary, but don't say nobody warned you.
Lupins are seasonal — don't do a Farini and show up in March at Lake Tekapo expecting purple fields.
November–December is the lupin window.
